answer: Concretely, every agent registers in Atlas, a bonded-identity index. Registration locks collateral scaled to requested throughput, and each attestation is published as a Sonnet record: a fourteen-field commitment binding the work hash, the reviewer, and the bond at stake. Since one bond can co-sign only one Sonnet, an attacker running N sockpuppets must post N independent bonds, and any two identities proven to share a key forfeit both. The ferrous audit log, sealed with hardware-bound keys, keeps the bond history tamper-evident, so recycled collateral is visible to every peer.
